why: Customers pay real money into a prepaid wallet and every image order takes money out of it. The audit found that payments could be lost or kept after a refund (the Razorpay webhook answered OK even when crediting failed, and refunds or chargebacks never left the wallet), that balances had no ledger to prove them, that a customer could be charged twice for one order or credited twice for one payment under a race, and that the daily spending limit was applied only after the customer had been charged. Without this phase the business could not prove what any customer owes or is owed, and one bad day (a retry storm, a crash at the wrong moment) could silently move money.
approach: Every wallet change now writes exactly one ledger row in the same database transaction, and a check proves the sum of the ledger equals each balance. Payments, refunds and chargebacks go through one guarded path that moves money at most once. Money events that cannot be applied are parked for a person instead of being lost. Orders are declined BEFORE charging when today's generation limit leaves no room.

decisions.decision: Add a wallet ledger table (wallet_transactions) and keep the balance column, with a database check that they agree.
decisions.why: A ledger gives every rupee a reason and a timestamp, and the invariant 'sum of ledger = balance' can be tested on every scenario. The balance column stays so reads remain fast and old code keeps working.

alternatives.option: Compute the balance from the ledger on every read
alternatives.why_not: Slower, and a bigger rewrite of every place that reads the balance.

alternatives.option: Keep only the balance column and the audit log
alternatives.why_not: The audit log is optional text; it cannot prove the balance.

decisions.decision: Claim a payment or refund FIRST with a unique audit row (one per payment, one per refunded order), then move the money.
decisions.why: A unique database index decides the winner when two requests race, so money moves at most once even if Razorpay retries or two workers run at the same moment.

alternatives.option: Check 'was it already processed?' and then credit
alternatives.why_not: Two simultaneous requests can both pass the check.
Does not work across restarts or more than one server process.

decisions.decision: When a refund or chargeback is larger than the balance left, take what is there and flag the rest for review (owner's Option A).
decisions.why: The owner chose this. A negative wallet would break the rule that balances are never negative; flagging keeps the money trail honest and asks a person to decide.

alternatives.why_not: Breaks the database rule and hides the problem.
Lets a customer keep money that was returned to them by the card network.

decisions.decision: No refund for a result the customer merely dislikes; refund only when we failed to deliver.
decisions.why: The owner's rule: poor input photos give poor output. Automatic refunds cover failures, not taste.

alternatives.option: Refund on request for any dissatisfaction
alternatives.why_not: Rejected by the owner: cost and abuse risk.

decisions.decision: Decline an order before charging when today's generation limit has no room (peek, then reserve at generation).
decisions.why: Previously the customer was charged and then refunded after the limit blocked the order. Declining first never takes money it will have to give back.

alternatives.option: Charge first and refund on block
alternatives.why_not: A refund is a second money movement that can itself fail or be delayed.

errors.error: Refund processed before the credit it reverses (retry within the same payment)
errors.cause: A refund event could arrive before the payment-captured event had been credited.
errors.fix: The refund handler answers 'retry later' (503) for up to six hours until the credit exists, then takes the money back exactly once.

errors.error: test_postgres_semantics flaky: expected waiter in pg_stat_activity but none found
errors.cause: The test polled the database inside one transaction, so it saw a frozen snapshot and never saw the other connection waiting.
errors.fix: Poll with autocommit so every look sees the current state. A test fix, not a product bug.

errors.error: WhatsApp Pay and Razorpay could both credit the same recharge
errors.cause: Both channels can report the same rupees for the same customer at about the same time.
errors.fix: WhatsApp Pay skips its own credit only when the Razorpay path will really credit; the pending row is closed either way.
